sections.heading: Overrides and overlays
sections.text: Pool assignment of performing exposures cannot be overridden; for defaulted exposures, FR&R may override the collateral value used for the ELBE only for three admissible reasons in a closed list (signed sale agreement, new full valuation not yet loaded, confirmed fraud), based on information not captured by the model. The override policy limits the change to the documented evidence value and requires approval by an FR&R senior credit officer independent of the case handler; positive overrides that lower the ELBE by more than 5 percentage points additionally require approval by Retail Credit Risk Management, making the policy more restrictive for favourable overrides. Every override is recorded in RECOV with reason code, written rationale, supporting evidence, proposer and approver. Override rates, direction and magnitude are monitored quarterly by reason and approving unit (2.1% of defaulted facilities in 2025, below the 5% retail threshold), and the performance of overridden cases is analysed annually by comparing realised LGD with the ELBE before and after override, including the performance of the approving officers. No overlays or post-model adjustments are applied to version 3.1; the model is complemented by human oversight through the review of FR&R case managers and the quarterly monitoring, which detect errors from model weaknesses using information not considered by the model.

sections.heading: Version and change history of the rating system
sections.text: The register of rating system versions in the model inventory records all current and historical versions with approvals, changes and dates: v1.0 (IRB permission December 2007), v2.0 (2016 redevelopment, permission 2017), v3.0 (2021 redevelopment for EBA/GL/2016/07, EBA/GL/2017/16 and EBA/GL/2019/03), v3.0.1 (2023, correction of the indirect cost allocation) and v3.1 (2025 recalibration). Version 3.0 was a material change requiring prior permission (Class A): it was validated before submission, approved by the Model Risk Committee on 15 June 2021 (decision MRC-2021-033, quorum including the Head of Model Validation), and material aspects of the rating process were approved by the Management Board on 29 June 2021 on the MRC recommendation. The application was submitted to the ECB on 30 July 2021, after internal approval; version 3.0 was used for own funds requirements only after the ECB permission of 2 November 2022 and was implemented on 31 January 2023, within three months of the notification of the permission. Version 3.1 was classified by the developer as internally non-material and regulatory Class C (RWEA impact −2.1% in the range of application and −0.3% at Bank level at 31 December 2024; no qualitative criterion met; the extension of the time series consists only of the inclusion of the most recent observations), and the classification was approved by MRM on 11 March 2025. Version 3.1 was approved by the model owner on 30 May 2025 after MRM's confirmation of the classification, recorded as a new version in the inventory, and notified to the ECB in the quarterly ex post notification of 15 October 2025.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This report documents the data quality (DQ) assessment of the reference data set LGDMORT_RDS_v2025.1 of the LGD model for Dutch residential mortgages (MDL-02), performed before the RDS was frozen for the recalibration of model version 3.1, as required by MRM-STD-022 section 5.1 for every new RDS version used for recalibration. The assessment covers all 41 RDS variables, all designated as critical data elements, and the 318 DQ rules defined jointly by the model developer and the Data Stewards of the Mortgage Lending, Credit Risk, Recovery and Collateral domains. Document version 1.0, approved by the model owner on 21 February 2025 after review by T. Jansen; author S. de Vries. The DQ assessment for the periodic validation is performed by Model Validation on its own validation data set and is not part of this report.

sections.heading: Data quality framework and rules
sections.text: The DQ rules cover the mandatory dimensions of MRM-STD-022 section 3 (completeness, accuracy, consistency and timeliness) and, where relevant, validity, uniqueness and appropriateness; for each critical data element at least one rule is defined per applicable dimension, and the reason is recorded where a dimension does not apply (for example timeliness for static contract data). Each rule has an amber and a red threshold; the default thresholds of MRM-STD-022 section 4.3 apply unless stricter thresholds are set. For the target variable and its constituents, the accuracy thresholds are 0.25% (amber) and 0.5% (red) of amounts, stricter than the defaults, and completeness thresholds are 99.5% and 99%. One deviation towards a less strict threshold applies: the timeliness rule for indirect cost bookings in RECOV, which are allocated quarterly by Finance, uses amber at the required refresh plus two months; the deviation is justified by the quarterly cost allocation cycle and was approved by the model owner and by Model Risk Management on 30 January 2025. The rules are implemented as recurring checks in the Group DQ monitoring tool, so that the same rules run monthly on the production input data of the LGD engine. The Bank's data quality management framework, formalised in DATA-POL-001 and MRM-STD-022, covers all data used in IRB-related processes, including the external house price and interest rate data used by this model.

sections.heading: Completeness
sections.text: Record-level completeness: all 34,912 default events in the default register with a default date between 2008 and 2023 and an in-scope product code are present in the raw RDS, and all recovery processes in RECOV are linked to a default event; 94 legacy default events without cash flows were identified (DD-LGDM-03). Attribute-level completeness is 100% for 33 of the 41 variables; the lowest values are valuation date at origination (96.9%, amber), indirect cost allocation for processes closed before 2012 (0%, recorded as deficiency DD-LGDM-02) and property type (98.6%). The completeness of default and recovery data, the main inputs for the realised LGD, is 100% from 2012 onwards. Where data are not complete, the gaps are explained and their effect on the LGD estimates is assessed in section 9 and in section 5.3 of the RDS documentation. All material risk data for the Dutch mortgage portfolio are captured, across all legal entities and business lines holding such exposures.

sections.heading: Accuracy and reconciliation
sections.text: Key amounts were reconciled with source systems and accounting data: outstanding amount at default with HYPO (difference 0.12%), write-offs with the general ledger (0.21%), recoveries with the RECOV ledger (0.04%) and NHG claim payments with the WEW settlement statements (0.09%); all results are green. Record counts per reference date were reconciled with the monthly default register extracts, and every default event was reconciled with the default register maintained under CR-STD-110, confirming the accuracy of the default flag. As required for Tier 1 models, a sample-based verification against source documentation was performed on 400 recovery files: seven date discrepancies (1.75%) were found and corrected at source, and no amount differences above EUR 100 were identified. Accuracy was further checked by comparing the house price index series with the published CBS figures and the EURIBOR fixings with the official publication, without differences. The reconciliations are performed on a largely automated basis by the reconciliation jobs of the credit risk data warehouse, which minimises the probability of errors.

sections.text: The data flow from HYPO, AMS, RECOV, CVD and the general ledger through the credit risk data warehouse to the RDS environment is part of the Bank's risk data architecture, which supports the monthly own funds calculation and ad hoc aggregation in stress situations. The risk data aggregation and reporting capabilities used for the model are governed under DATA-POL-001, approved by the Management Board, and were reviewed by Internal Audit's data and IT specialists in audit IA-2024-032 (BCBS 239 compliance). Ownership of each data domain rests with a single Data Owner recorded in the Group Data Catalogue, and the data quality expectations for the critical data elements were agreed between the model owner and the Data Owners in DQA-LGDM-2025. documents.title: Implementation and testing report LGD Mortgages v3.1

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This report documents the implementation and testing of version 3.1 of the LGD model for Dutch residential mortgages (MDL-02) in the regulatory capital engine (RCE) and the monthly LGD production run, carried out between 14 April and 20 June 2025 before the go-live on 30 June 2025. Version 3.1 is a recalibration of version 3.0 without changes to the model structure, drivers or default definition; the implementation changes are the new parameter table PT-LGDM-3.1, the new pool boundaries and the updated MoC values. The implementation specification IS-LGDM-3.1 v1.0 was prepared from the approved MDD and approved by the model owner on 14 April 2025, before implementation started. Document version 1.0, author: Risk IT Test Centre (lead tester P. Hendriks), reviewed by the model developer, approved by the model owner on 20 June 2025.

evidence.quote: This report documents the implementation and testing of version 3.1 of the LGD model for Dutch residential mortgages (MDL-02) in the regulatory capital engine (RCE) and the monthly LGD production run, carried out between 14 April and 20 June 2025 before the go-live on 30 June 2025.
The implementation specification IS-LGDM-3.1 v1.0 was prepared from the approved MDD and approved by the model owner on 14 April 2025, before implementation started.

sections.heading: Implementation specification
sections.text: The specification defines for every input variable the production source field and its lineage in the credit risk data warehouse and identifies the differences between development and production data sources: in production the indexed LTV is taken from the CVD monthly index run rather than recomputed from the index file, which gives identical values. It defines every transformation, the missing value and outlier treatments (conservative default for missing valuation, capping of indexed LTV at 250%), the formulas of the P(cure), LGC and LGL components, all coefficients, the pool boundaries, the downturn and MoC parameters, the 5% floor and the override rules for defaulted exposures, with a precision of 10 decimals and rounding of the final LGD to four decimals. The specification includes 1,240 test cases with expected outputs produced with the development code, covering typical cases, boundary values of each pool, missing and invalid inputs, every calibration segment and pool, and defaulted exposures at every reference date in default. The lineage of development data and production input data was compared, and the only difference (indexed LTV source) was shown to have no effect on outputs.

The production code changes were reviewed by a developer of Risk IT other than the author and approved in change request CHG-2025-11873 before deployment. The parameter table PT-LGDM-3.1 is version controlled, access is restricted to the RCE parameter administrators, and changes are possible only through change management. Model developers have read-only access to the production environment and cannot deploy code or parameters. The change was recorded in the change log of the model inventory on 11 March 2025, before its implementation in production.

sections.heading: Implementation testing
sections.text: Testing was performed by the Risk IT Test Centre, which is independent of the production code author and of the model development team, as required for a Tier 1 model. The tests covered all 1,240 specified test cases, the mapping of input data and transformations, the handling of missing, invalid and boundary values and the outputs for every calibration segment and pool. Test plan, cases, results and defects are documented in test report TR-LGDM-3.1; four defects were found (two in the rounding of the pool boundary comparison, one in the override log and one in a report label), and the three affecting outputs were resolved and retested before go-live. The organisation-wide testing process of Risk IT, documented in the IRB systems test procedure, applies to the first implementation and to every subsequent change of the IRB systems and applications. The test of the RCE risk weight calculation confirmed that the retail residential mortgage risk weight formula is applied correctly with the new LGD values, including the 5% LGD floor and the input floor for PD.

sections.heading: Reconciliation with development outputs
sections.text: Production outputs were reconciled at record level with the outputs of the development code on identical input data covering the full RDS (31,206 default events at all reference dates) and the performing portfolio at 31 March 2025 (366,904 facilities). All continuous outputs agree within an absolute difference of 2.1 x 10^-9, well within the tolerance of 10^-6, and the pool assignment is identical for all records. No differences outside tolerance occurred, so no investigation was needed and go-live was not blocked. The model outputs were reconciled with the downstream systems consuming them (the COREP reporting database, the pricing tool and the IFRS 9 engine) at go-live, and the reconciliation is repeated annually; the reconciliation of December 2025 showed no differences. The lineage comparison and the output reconciliation confirm that development and production are consistent.

sections.heading: Parallel run
sections.text: Although version 3.1 is a non-material change, a parallel run of version 3.0 and 3.1 was performed for the production cycles of 31 March, 30 April and 31 May 2025, as recommended for IRB models by MRM-STD-030 section 7.1. Results: 71.4% of facilities remain in the same pool, 16.2% move one pool lower and 12.1% one pool higher; the EAD-weighted average LGD decreases from 9.9% to 9.6% and the RWEA of the range of application decreases by 2.1%, in line with the impact reported in the change classification. No operational issues occurred during the three cycles; run times increased by four minutes because of the additional reference date output. The parallel run results were discussed with Regulatory Reporting and Capital Management before go-live.

Manual reruns, manual output adjustments and the fallback procedure (use of the previous month's pool assignment in case of a run failure) are documented in the run book, authorised by the RCE owner and logged; no manual adjustment was made in 2025. Model outputs used for regulatory reporting are retained with the input data and the code version for ten years. Emergency changes deployed before completion of all tests require approval by the model owner and MRM and completion of the outstanding tests within 30 calendar days; no emergency change was made to the model.

sections.heading: Post-implementation review
sections.text: A post-implementation review was performed on 12 December 2025, comparing the realised impact on the portfolio of 30 September 2025 (RWEA −2.3% in the range of application) with the estimated impact (−2.1%); the difference is explained by portfolio growth in low-LTV pools. The review was reported to MRM together with the confirmation that the production code, the implementation specification and the MDD remain consistent. Any future difference between production code and the MDD or implementation specification will be treated as a defect or submitted as a model change under MRM-STD-050. sections.heading: Portfolio overview
sections.text: At 31 December 2025 the range of application contains 368,512 facilities of 341,870 obligors with an EAD of EUR 61.8 billion and an RWEA of EUR 7.1 billion; the portfolio at the start of the observation period (31 December 2024) contained 366,120 facilities with an EAD of EUR 60.9 billion. During 2025, 1,262 facilities defaulted (0.34%), and 1,318 recovery processes were closed, of which 1,041 cures, 244 sales and 33 other closures. Model coverage: 100.0% of the in-scope EAD received a model LGD; 0.02% of facilities (74) used the conservative default for a missing valuation, all resolved within the following month, and no outputs are outdated. The new product 'home improvement loan part for energy measures', introduced in April 2025, was assessed for the continued appropriateness of the model: it is secured by the same mortgage deed and is assigned to the pool of the facility, so no change to the model is needed.

sections.heading: Back-testing of LGD, ELBE and cure rates
sections.text: Realised LGDs of the 1,318 recovery processes closed in 2025 were compared with the estimated LGD per pool and for the portfolio; in no pool does the realised LGD exceed the estimate, and the portfolio shows no underestimation. Component-level back-testing shows a realised cure rate above the predicted P(cure) in all pools and a realised LGL of 23.4% against an estimated LGL of 27.9% for liquidations. The ELBE was back-tested against realised LGD for defaulted exposures at the reference dates in default, with no significant difference at portfolio or pool level. The back-test is performed on the whole application portfolio, without the exclusions or adjustments of the development, and the discriminatory power per period is compared with development. Realised values have not exceeded estimates in any year since 2016, so no upward revision of the estimates is required.

sections.heading: Annual review of estimates
sections.text: The annual review included the 1,338 defaults of 2024 in a recalculation of the long-run average: the LRA LGD changes from 8.5% to 8.4% and the downturn LGD is unchanged, so recent data do not materially change the estimates. The representativeness of the RDS for the application portfolio was re-assessed, including portfolio changes and structural breaks: no structural break was identified, and the PSI of indexed LTV increased to 0.21. The review concluded that no recalibration is required, that the MoC remains adequate and that the model remains fit for purpose. Data adjustment and exclusion policies were applied to the review datasets in the same way as to the RDS. The review of the downturn identification in January 2026 confirmed DP-A and DP-B, as no indicator reached a more severe 12-month value in 2025.

sections.heading: Overrides and default definition monitoring
sections.text: Overrides of collateral values for defaulted exposures: 46 overrides in 2025 (2.1% of defaulted facilities), of which 39 for signed sale agreements and 7 for new valuations, 31 lowering and 15 increasing the ELBE, with an average absolute change of 2.8 percentage points; all were approved by FR&R senior credit officers independent of the case handlers. Realised LGDs of overridden cases closed in 2025 are closer to the post-override ELBE than to the pre-override ELBE (mean absolute error 3.1 against 6.4 percentage points), confirming that overrides improve accuracy; no systematic pattern per approving officer was found. The effectiveness of the return-to-non-default policy was monitored: 8.9% of the obligors cured in 2023 re-defaulted within 12 months, in line with previous years. Early-warning indicators for the mortgage portfolio (payment arrears, BKR registrations, loss of income) triggered 3,412 reviews in 2025, all assessed within 30 days.

sections.heading: Management reporting and use
sections.text: The quarterly IRB report to the Credit Risk Committee and the Model Risk Committee presents for MDL-02 the risk profile by pool, migration across pools, LGD estimates per pool, the comparison of realised with estimated LGD and the outcome of the ICAAP stress test, in which LGD increases to 17.8% under the severe scenario. The report also states the materiality of the rating system, its perceived strengths and limitations and its status in light of validation and audit actions. Senior management and the Management Board are informed of material changes and exceptions; the CRO presented the 2025 review to the Management Board on 24 March 2026, and the members of the Management Board attended a session on the design and operation of the IRB rating systems in September 2025. The credit risk stress test, based on severe but plausible recession scenarios and covering all IRB portfolios, assessed pool migration and its effect on own funds requirements: the RWEA of the mortgage portfolio increases by 38% under the severe scenario. Reports are reconciled with the COREP data before distribution and cover all material risk areas of the portfolio.

sections.heading: Governance, credit risk control and audit
sections.text: Retail Credit Risk Modelling is part of the credit risk control unit within the Risk function, independent of Retail Mortgages, which originates and renews exposures, and reports through the Head of Credit Risk Modelling to the CRO. The unit is responsible for the design, implementation, oversight and performance of the rating system, participates in its validation through the provision of data and responses to findings, and reviews the model on an ongoing basis through this monitoring; it has 14 FTE, adequate for the retail rating systems in scope. Internal Audit reviewed the retail IRB rating systems in audit IA-2025-017 (October 2025), covering the estimation of LGD, the validation function and adherence to the IRB requirements; the audit plan follows from Internal Audit's annual risk assessment of all aspects of the rating systems. Documentation and evidence of continued compliance of the rating system are maintained in the model file to support the ECB's regular review of internal approaches. The 2025 supervisory benchmarking submission followed the templates, definitions and IT solutions of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2070.

sections.heading: Summary and validation opinion
sections.text: Model Validation – Credit Risk performed the annual validation 2026 of the LGD model for Dutch residential mortgages (MDL-02, version 3.1) on the submission package SUB-MDL-02-20260612, with observation period 1 January to 31 December 2025. The validation opinion is Fit for purpose with conditions: the model ranks risk adequately, estimates are conservative in back-testing and the downturn and MoC framework complies with EBA/GL/2017/16 and EBA/GL/2019/03, but the MoC for the approximated default flag is insufficient and the representativeness of the RDS for maturity-driven defaults of interest-only loans has not been demonstrated. In the ECB reporting scale the overall assessment corresponds to minor deficiencies, since the estimated RWEA impact of all findings together (+1.4%) is below the ±5% threshold for major deficiencies. The model is not assessed as materially non-compliant, and its use for own funds requirements can continue subject to the conditions in section 13. The opinion is formed by aggregating the results of the individual analyses with the weighting scheme of the validation policy MV-STD-001, in which findings in risk quantification weigh more than presentational findings.

sections.text: The validation was performed by P. Bakker and L. Smit of Model Validation – Credit Risk, who did not contribute to the development of the model in the preceding two years and whose remuneration is not linked to model approval. Model Validation is organisationally independent of the credit risk control unit and of Retail Mortgages: it reports to the Chief Risk Officer through the Head of Model Risk Management, a different member of senior management than the Head of Credit Risk Modelling, and it reports its findings to senior management. The team of nine validators for credit risk IRB models has the seniority and expertise needed to challenge the credit risk control unit effectively. The validation covers all components of the rating system (data, default definition, design, risk quantification including downturn and MoC, pool assignment, implementation and use), at the consolidated and solo level at which the rating system is approved, and completes the annual cycle following the full-scope validation of July 2025. The validation policy lists each analysis with purpose, limitations, scope, frequency and, for quantitative tests, targets and tolerance thresholds, and differentiates procedures by materiality and complexity of the rating system. No validation tasks were outsourced.

sections.text: Model Validation formed its own opinion on the data quality dimensions and processes: the DQ framework is adequate, the RDS is complete, and data cleansing is appropriate; the deficiencies DD-LGDM-01 to -05 bias the parameters only to the extent covered by MoC, except DD-LGDM-01 (see finding F-01). The default definition applied in the RDS and in production complies with CRR Article 178, EBA/GL/2016/07 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171, including thresholds, UTP triggers, probation and contagion, as confirmed on the RDS build code and the AMS default logic. sections.heading: Methodology and model design
sections.text: The component design with cure and liquidation paths is appropriate for Dutch residential mortgages; model specifications were challenged by re-estimating the P(cure) and LGL components on 2016–2023 defaults, which yields coefficients within two standard errors of the development values. The last full-scope validation of July 2025 assessed alternative modelling possibilities for the key methodological choices, including a survival model of recoveries, and reviewed analyses not performed in the annual validations. Model Validation reviewed the materiality classification of the changes since the last validation (version 3.1, Class C) and agrees with the classification, also considering their combined effect. Discriminatory power and homogeneity within and heterogeneity between pools are adequate: the gAUC on the 2025 closed processes is 0.691 against 0.702 at development, and adjacent pools remain statistically distinct.

sections.heading: Downturn LGD
sections.text: Model Validation challenged the identification of the economic downturn under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/930: the nature (relevant indicator set including the provincial house price indices), the severity (20-year span, extension assessment) and the duration (merged period DP-B of 31 months) are adequately justified. The downturn LGD of each segment exceeds the realised LGDs of defaults in the downturn period DP-B and the reference value. The downturn calibration on observed impact is coherent with the impact analysis; independently recomputed downturn LGD best estimates differ from the developer's figures by less than 0.05 percentage points. The ELBE contains neither MoC nor other conservative adjustments, as verified in the production code.

sections.heading: Margin of conservatism
sections.text: Model Validation assessed whether Category A and B MoC cover all identified deficiencies and Category C covers the general estimation error. Model Validation's own sensitivity analysis of DD-LGDM-01 re-estimated the LRA under three alternative approximations of the historical default flag (60 days past due at month-end, 90 days past due on a daily approximation from monthly arrears, and the exclusion of 2008–2011 cures without probation), resulting in effects of +0.30, +0.47 and +0.52 percentage points; the applied MoC A1 of +0.30 percentage points does not cover the plausible range (finding F-01, Medium). Category C MoC was reproduced with Model Validation's own bootstrap (5,000 replications, obligor resampling) within 0.01 percentage points. The other MoC components are adequate, and the order of application of downturn, MoC and floor is identical in development and production.

sections.heading: Back-testing and calibration
sections.text: LGD back-testing on the 1,318 recovery processes closed in 2025 with a one-sided paired t-test of realised versus estimated LGD shows no underestimation at portfolio level or in any pool (portfolio p > 0.99), and back-testing on all cases including estimated future recoveries of the 1,788 incomplete processes confirms the result. Estimated future recoveries of incomplete processes at the end of 2024 were compared with the recoveries realised in 2025: realised recoveries were 101.8% of the estimate. The ELBE back-test with a two-sided paired t-test at portfolio and pool level and at the reference dates of 6, 12 and 24 months in default shows no significant deviation (p between 0.21 and 0.64). The statistical tests are documented in the validation policy, use the regulatory LGD definitions and all available data, are run at portfolio, segment and pool level, and include the performance in the 2012–2014 downturn period. All quantitative analyses have thresholds, and none of the threshold breaches (PSI of indexed LTV, amber) requires further measures beyond monitoring.

sections.heading: Representativeness and stability
sections.text: Representativeness of the development sample for the application portfolio was analysed for scope, definition of default, risk characteristics, lending standards and recovery policies. The shift of the indexed LTV distribution is adequately explained, but interest-only loans originated before 2013 (31% of EAD) will reach contractual maturity from 2030 onwards, and the RDS contains no defaults at maturity, whose cure probability and loss levels may differ materially from defaults during the term (finding F-03, Medium). Pool stability was analysed with migration matrices for 2021–2025: 88% of facilities remain in the same pool within a year, and migration towards lower pools reflects rising house prices, consistent with the point-in-time sensitivity of indexed LTV.

sections.heading: Benchmarking and use test
sections.text: The model was benchmarked against Model Validation's challenger (a beta regression on the same RDS, gAUC 0.684) and against the WEW loss statistics for NHG loans, and the 2025 supervisory benchmarking results were reviewed; differences are explained by portfolio composition. The use test was confirmed: the LGD is used in pricing, risk appetite, the ICAAP and management reporting. Overrides of collateral values for defaulted exposures (2.1% of defaulted facilities, 0.3% of defaulted EAD, negligible RWEA effect) were assessed for materiality and the maximum acceptable override rate of 5% was reviewed and found appropriate. Model performance before and after overrides was compared: the post-override ELBE predicts realised LGD better than the pre-override ELBE.

sections.heading: Implementation and code review
sections.text: Model Validation reviewed the RDS build code (tag v3.1.0), the estimation code (tag v3.1.2) and the RCE production code (tag v3.1.0) against the MDD and RDS documentation and re-ran 200 test cases on an independently drawn sample. The production implementation reproduces the documented model exactly, and the user acceptance tests of June 2025 were concluded without material errors. One inconsistency was found in the RDS build code: module discounting.py floors the 3-month EURIBOR at 0% before adding the 5 percentage point add-on (line 57), whereas section 4.4.2 of the RDS documentation states that the fixing is used as observed; the effect on the LRA LGD is +0.04 percentage points (finding F-02, Medium). Data sources, variables and risk drivers are properly documented in the RDS documentation and the implementation specification.

sections.heading: ECB validation reporting
sections.text: The validation tools of the ECB instructions were applied to the rating system approved at the start of the observation period, covering all facilities in its range of application, using the one-year observation period 1 January to 31 December 2025. Portfolio information for the beginning and end of the observation period (RWEA, EAD, number of facilities, number of pools and number of defaults) is reported in template section 2.4.3. The templates were named according to the convention [LEICode]_[ModelType]_[ModelID]_[ReferenceDate]_[VersionNumber] with reference date 31122025, reconciled with the internal validation data and COREP exposures, four-eyes reviewed and signed off by the Head of Model Validation. The templates are submitted to the ECB together with this annual validation report at consolidated level, and the report is shared with the ECB within one month after its approval. The time from the reference date of the data (31 December 2025) to the approval of the validation results (MRC meeting of 21 July 2026) is less than one year.

sections.heading: Findings and conditions
sections.text: The findings are listed with severity, materiality and the related requirements, so that the credit risk control unit can prioritise remediation: F-01 (Medium) MoC A1 insufficient, condition to increase A1 to at least +0.55 percentage points by 30 September 2026; F-02 (Medium) discount rate floor in the build code inconsistent with documentation, to be aligned by 30 September 2026; F-03 (Medium) representativeness for defaults at maturity of interest-only loans, analysis and, where needed, MoC by 30 September 2026; F-04 (Low) separate documentation of the ELBE adjustment to current economic circumstances, by 30 September 2026. The combined effect of the findings on the performance and regulatory usability of the rating system is limited: the estimated RWEA impact is +1.4%, and the model remains usable for own funds requirements. Condition C-2026-LGDM-01 (F-01) was entered in the MRC conditions register on 15 July 2026 with owner (model owner) and deadline (30 September 2026); closure evidence is to be submitted before the deadline and confirmed by Model Validation. The model owner is required to submit remediation plans for the three Medium findings within 20 business days of this report.

sections.heading: Reporting and governance
sections.text: The validation conclusions, findings and recommendations are reported to senior management and to the Model Risk Committee, and are addressed through the findings remediation process with follow-up by Model Validation. The outcome of this Tier 1 validation was presented to the MRC on 21 July 2026, with the aggregated summary of validation results across the IRB rating systems, including exceeded thresholds and identified deficiencies, provided to the Management Board. The meeting papers, including this report, the validation opinion, the 1LoD self-assessment, the open findings and the proposed condition, were distributed on 14 July 2026, five business days before the meeting. The model owner accepted all findings; no disagreement had to be escalated to the MRC. Report approved by the Head of Model Validation on 10 July 2026 after review by a senior validator outside the validation team.

deficiencies.rationale: 94 defaults of the former brand portfolio (2008–2010) are excluded from LGD quantification because facility-level cash flows are missing; the effect is estimated at +0.03 percentage points and covered by MoC A4, but EBA/GL/2017/16 para 163 does not permit excluding observed defaults from quantification.

mitigation.text: Retrieve the recovery amounts of the 94 legacy defaults from the archived FR&R case files or include them with a conservative realised LGD (for example the 90th percentile of comparable defaults) instead of excluding them.

deficiencies.rationale: The MDD states that the ELBE reflects current economic circumstances through the indexed LTV, but does not demonstrate that realised LGDs are sensitive to this driver at the reference dates in default, nor document separately why no adjustment of the long-run average is needed.

mitigation.text: Add to section 5.6 the analysis of the sensitivity of the ELBE to current house prices and document the conclusion on the need for an adjustment to current economic circumstances separately.

deficiencies.rationale: The comparison of the current pool distribution with the distribution under DP-B house prices shows a material shift (34% of EAD to higher pools), but the conclusion that no adjustment is required is not supported by a quantification of the effect on the downturn LGD.

mitigation.text: Quantify the downturn LGD of the current portfolio under the DP-B pool distribution and document whether an adjustment to limit cyclicality is required.

deficiencies.rationale: MoC A1 for the approximated default flag is supported by a sensitivity analysis with a single alternative treatment (+0.30 pp). Model Validation's independent sensitivity analysis with three plausible alternative approximations shows effects of up to +0.52 pp, so the applied MoC does not cover the plausible range of the deficiency.

mitigation.text: Increase MoC A1 to at least +0.55 percentage points in both calibration segments and extend the sensitivity analysis to the full set of plausible alternative approximations.

deficiencies.rationale: Representativeness is demonstrated on risk-driver distributions and loss levels for the observed defaults, but interest-only loans originated before 2013 (31% of EAD) reach maturity from 2030 and the RDS contains no defaults at contractual maturity, whose cure probability and loss levels may differ materially; the validation's outcome-level comparison could not be performed for this sub-population.

mitigation.text: Analyse the expected cure and loss behaviour of defaults at maturity of interest-only loans (for example using maturity-driven defaults of bridge and consumer loans and expert panel input) and add a Category B MoC or pool adjustment where the RDS is not representative.
